lessonInfo.title: How Can Robots Use Sensors and Decision-Making Logic to Navigate Their Environment?

standards.description: Use program design problem-solving strategies to create program solutions
Design a solution to a problem
Develop algorithms to decision-making problems using branching control statements

learningObjectives: Explain how robots use sensor input to make decisions
Design a branching logic algorithm for robot navigation
Collaboratively debug and improve robot behaviors
Apply computational thinking to real-world robotics systems
successCriteria: Students can explain the relationship between inputs, decisions, and outputs
Students can create a basic branching logic flowchart
Students can identify and debug flaws in an algorithm
Students can collaboratively explain their reasoning

extensions: Add multiple sensors to robot logic

circulateFocus: Ask students to explain reasoning clearly
Push groups to consider edge cases
Check for participation from all group members

phases.title: How Do Robots Know What To Do?
phases.prompt: Watch the robot navigation demo. How do you think the robot decides when to stop, turn, or move forward?
instructions: Submit one prediction as a group
Be ready to explain your reasoning
keyActions: Listen carefully to the robot's behavior
Discuss what sensory information could guide decisions

phases.title: Sensors, Inputs, and Branching Logic
keyIdeas: Sensors provide robots with information about their environment
Input from sensors allows robots to make decisions
Branching logic (IF/THEN) helps robots respond to different situations
Autonomous systems combine sensing, decisions, and actions
Good algorithms handle multiple scenarios and edge cases

phases.title: Design the Robot Logic
phases.prompt: Your team has been hired to help a robot navigate an environment safely. Create a decision-making algorithm using sensor inputs and branching logic.
instructions: Create a flowchart or pseudocode solution
keyActions: Collaborate and listen to your teammates' ideas
Break down the problem into clear decision points
Test your logic against different scenarios
Document your reasoning for each branch
Consider what happens if sensors give unexpected data

phases.title: Debug the Broken Robot
phases.prompt: Your robot algorithm contains bugs. Identify what is failing and revise the logic so the robot behaves correctly.
keyActions: Identify where the logic breaks down
Find the root cause of the error
Propose a fix and test it mentally
Learn from the mistake to strengthen your understanding

phases.title: Class Debrief and Solution Sharing
discussionPrompts: What types of mistakes appeared most often?
Why is debugging important in robotics?
How do engineers improve reliability in autonomous systems?
keyIdeas: Different valid approaches can solve the same problem
Debugging is a core engineering skill, not just fixing errors
Edge cases and error conditions must be planned for
Real-world systems require robust, reliable decision-making

phases.title: Exit Reflection
reflectionQuestions: What role do sensors play in robotics?
How does branching logic help robots make decisions?
What debugging strategy helped your team most today?
What improvement would you make to your algorithm?
keyActions: Reflect honestly on what you learned today
Think about how sensors and logic connect to real robotics
Consider what debugging strategy worked best for your team
Identify one thing you would improve in your algorithm
Recognize your growth in computational thinking
